note: G96. G95 nulled the selector in AGGREGATE and G88 publishes it as a frozen PER-KEY table with a sha256. This fits the same selector independently on two disjoint shuffled halves of validation and measures how often they choose the same arm for the same key, against a chance rate computed from the observed marginals rather than assumed at 1/5.

controls.name: reproduces_g88
controls.must_fire_because: nothing here is about G88 unless its headline reproduces from its own instrument
controls.can_fail_because: a moved embedding, a changed miner, a different split
controls.null_must_contain: a different mrr -- the pipeline is re-run from corpus and embeddings, so any drift in the arms or the split misses

controls.name: halves_disjoint_and_shuffled
controls.must_fire_because: A27: a hold-out drawn from one end of the key order is not a sample
controls.can_fail_because: the two index sets intersect, or the permutation is the identity
controls.null_must_contain: an overlap, or an unshuffled split. Taking valid_rows[:half] instead would put low predicate ids in A and high in B and is reachable by deleting one line

controls.name: chance_computed_from_marginals
controls.must_fire_because: a skewed choice distribution makes two independent selectors agree far more than 1/5, so the baseline must come from the data
controls.can_fail_because: the marginals come out uniform, which would make the naive baseline correct after all
controls.null_must_contain: a value far from 0.20. distmult holds 279/446 of the full table, so sum(p^2) must land well above a naive fifth -- if it did not, the marginals would be flat and the correction unnecessary

falsifiers.name: F1_per_key_choice_is_noise
falsifiers.can_fail_because: half-A and half-B agree at or below the chance rate computed from the observed marginals
falsifiers.null_must_contain: both answers -- agreement is measured and chance is measured, on the same keys
falsifiers.refutes: refutes any per-key reading of G88's frozen table and of G95's aggregate verdict: the choice at a key would flip on different validation data
falsifiers.fires_when: half-A and half-B agree at or below the chance rate computed from the observed marginals
falsifiers.verdict: survived — the falsifier did not fire

falsifiers.name: F2_selector_needs_full_validation
falsifiers.can_fail_because: neither half-fit selector beats DistMult on test
falsifiers.null_must_contain: both answers -- the half-fit MRRs and the DistMult baseline are computed from the same test rows
falsifiers.refutes: refutes the mechanism reading: if HALF the validation set cannot beat one arm, the published gain is partly a data-budget effect and is optimistic for any smaller validation set
falsifiers.fires_when: neither half-fit selector beats DistMult on test
falsifiers.verdict: survived — the falsifier did not fire

falsifiers.name: F3_g88_not_reproduced
falsifiers.null_must_contain: both answers; C1 gates on the same comparison
falsifiers.verdict: survived — the falsifier did not fire

falsifier: If the two halves agreed at or below the marginal chance rate, the per-key table would be validation noise and neither G88's choice_sha256 nor G95's aggregate verdict could be quoted about any individual key.
